extracted.intended_audience: NIH applicants, PIs, research administrators, and grant-watchers following NIH award timing
extracted.subtask_description: Heuristics and observational rules for inferring NIH R01 funding cycles and an institute's funding catch-up strategy from award project end dates and award-date distributions. Useful for applicants and analysts trying to determine which review Cycle an award belongs to and whether an IC is catching up on missed awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants Management spreads end dates across the Cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants Management issues end dates across the Cycle instead of always ending on the day before the first possible start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: "to spread out the workload dealing with issuing the out years (the noncompeting years of the project)." Example: PIs may request a 4/1 start but receive an award with a 3/31 end date. Treat uneven end-date assignment as an administrative scheduling practice rather than a strict indicator of the requested start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1/31 and 2/28 end dates likely indicate Cycle I awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The bulk of awards with 1/31 and 2/28 end dates are inferred to be Cycle I awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use counts of awards with 1/31 and 2/28 ends to estimate how many Cycle I awards an IC has actually issued (example: author counted ~23 such awards for NIDA). Caveat: this is an assumption based on observed patterns, not an official rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3/31 end dates likely indicate Cycle II awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards having annual end dates of 3/31 are very likely the Cycle II awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed example: seven new R01s awarded by NIDA on 6/1 had 3/31 end dates; two additional awards made mid-April to mid-May also had 3/31 end dates. Use 3/31 frequency as a heuristic for identifying Cycle II funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Some end-dates may be reserved for first start-dates of Cycles (3/31, 6/30, 11/30)
rubrics_metrics.description: 3/31, 6/30 and 11/30 end dates may be reserved for the first start date of the respective Cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret occurrences of these end-dates as possibly indicating awards aligned with the first start-date windows of different cycles; this helps map awards into cycle buckets when analyzing award timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late-September spike signals fiscal-year finishing behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: A relatively large proportion of new R01s issued between 9/15 and 9/30 can indicate finishing out the fiscal year (example: 32.6% of annual new R01s issued in that late-September window for FY2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret a late-September concentration as evidence that an IC may be clearing backlog or finishing awards at fiscal-year end; it can imply that only the top-ranked grants were funded on-cycle earlier, with others deferred to end-of-year pickups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare end-date counts across time and institutes to assess catch-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Counting awards with cycle-associated end dates and comparing those counts to prior-year totals or expected yearly totals is a way to assess whether an IC is catching up for missed Cycle awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the post: NIDA — author contrasts 7 awards with start dates before 4/1 vs an inferred 27 Cycle I/II awards by counting 1/31/2/28/12/31/3/31 end dates; NIAAA — of 21 awards in FY24, nine with 3/31 and five with 4/30, compared to ~110 new R01s issued in FY23. Use such comparisons as a heuristic measure of progress toward normal award volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requested start dates may not equal awarded project period boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs may request particular start dates (e.g., 4/1) but the awarded project periods can be issued with adjacent end dates (e.g., 3/31).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting award listings, do not assume the requested start date equals the awarded project period; administrative adjustments to project periods are common and affect how awards map to cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect exceptions and treat heuristics with caution
rubrics_metrics.description: The author notes vague memories of exceptions (e.g., a May 31 end to a Cycle III award) and admits uncertainty about past practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are observational heuristics rather than definitive rules. Verify unusual cases with Grants Management or official institute communications rather than relying solely on end-date inference.
